summary: Published node1’s release tree as the read-only `releases` rsync module. Node2 retrieves the complete tree with modes and symlinks intact. Writes, the private sibling, and traversal outside the module are denied. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot IDs. The OS release and kernel remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL-supported rsync 3.5.0 packages; the package dependency transaction also upgraded libacl on both nodes.
Configured rsyncd with chroot, read-only access, and node2-only admission.
Limited TCP/873 in firewalld to node2 and applied a read-only SELinux content label only to the release tree.
Verified full archive retrieval, file modes, checksums, and `current -> v1` symlink preservation.
Verified upload, private-module, and path-traversal denials.
Removed temporary test material and audited listeners, services, SELinux, firewall, packages, and protected data.
Restarted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Use software compatible with the installed legacy platform while retaining OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: RHEL 10 repository packages rsync/rsync-daemon 3.5.0-3.el10_2 were installed. Final audits retain RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.

evidence.requirement: Publish a read-only module named releases on node1 with narrowly scoped security controls
evidence.summary: The module is chrooted to the release directory, explicitly read-only, allowed only from node2, enabled at boot, protected by a source-specific firewall rule, and uses a narrowly scoped SELinux label while write/full-access booleans remain off.

evidence.requirement: Node2 retrieves the full tree with file modes and symlinks intact
evidence.summary: Both initial and final post-restart archive transfers retrieved 2 files, 3 directories, and 1 symlink; mode 0755, mode 0644, `current -> v1`, and both file hashes were verified.

evidence.requirement: Writes through the module and access outside its tree are denied
evidence.summary: Uploads returned `module is read only`; `private` returned `Unknown module`; traversal resolved inside the chroot and failed. Node1 confirmed no probe files were created.
Final release and private-canary hashes, modes, ownership, sizes, and symlink target match the pre-change baselines on both nodes.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Boot ID changed from 22045032-4379-47d6-bbf6-319fdca89750 to 97fd7428-0b06-4c0f-ba41-9b413081fd81. Rsyncd, listener, firewall, labels, data, retrieval, and denial behavior recovered.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node2 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Boot ID changed from 368725cb-c64e-4393-b25f-da5111703b4a to 896f3799-abc8-4666-a80f-3fc65e37ea56. The client, protected data, administrative services, and complete end-to-end workflow recovered.

No introduced temporary residue remains. SSH/firewalld are active, SELinux is enforcing, node2 has no rsync listener, node1 exposes only the intended rsync listener behind its restricted rule, and no rsync AVC denials were recorded.
